prompt: Provide the Android `network_security_config.xml` for an application that talks to an external API backend.
raw_response:
# Android network_security_config.xml

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<network-security-config>
    <!--
        Rule set: AGENT_RULES §3 (Binary Trust) — no cleartext HTTP anywhere,
        no user-installed CAs, no debug overrides in release.
    -->
    <base-config cleartextTrafficPermitted="false">
        <trust-anchors>
            <!-- Only system CAs are trusted. User-installed CAs (e.g., from
                 a rooted device or corporate MITM proxy) are explicitly
                 rejected. -->
            <certificates src="system" />
        </trust-anchors>
    </base-config>

    <!--
        Pin the external API backend. Replace the placeholder SPKI hashes
        with the actual SubjectPublicKeyInfo (SPKI) SHA-256 digests of the
        backend's leaf and/or intermediate certificates, base64-encoded.

        To generate:
          openssl s_client -connect api.example.com:443 -servername api.example.com \
            | openssl x509 -pubkey -noout \
            | openssl pkey -pubin -outform der \
            | openssl dgst -sha256 -binary \
            | openssl enc -base64

        Include at least two pins (one backup) to allow safe rotation.
    -->
    <domain-config cleartextTrafficPermitted="false">
        <domain includeSubdomains="false">api.example.com</domain>
        <trust-anchors>
            <certificates src="system" />
        </trust-anchors>
        <pin-set expiration="2026-12-31">
            <pin digest="SHA-256">REPLACE_WITH_BACKEND_SPKI_HASH_1</pin>
            <pin digest="SHA-256">REPLACE_WITH_BACKEND_SPKI_HASH_2</pin>
        </pin-set>
    </domain-config>

    <!--
        Explicitly deny any other cleartext domain. This is defense-in-depth;
        base-config already blocks cleartext globally.
    -->
    <domain-config cleartextTrafficPermitted="false">
        <domain includeSubdomains="true">example.com</domain>
    </domain-config>
</network-security-config>
```

---

## Manifest wiring

Ensure the manifest references this file and explicitly disables cleartext:

```xml
<application
    android:networkSecurityConfig="@xml/network_security_config"
    android:usesCleartextTraffic="false"
    ... >
</application>
```

---

## Security decisions stated

- **No cleartext HTTP anywhere** — `cleartextTrafficPermitted="false"` at base and per-domain, plus `usesCleartextTraffic="false"` in the manifest.
- **User-installed CAs rejected** — only `src="system"` trust anchors, preventing MITM via attacker-installed certificates on rooted devices.
- **Certificate pinning enforced** for the API backend with two SPKI pins and an expiration date to force rotation.
- **No debug overrides** — this file is release-safe; no `debug-overrides` element that could weaken TLS in debuggable builds.
